topic: JSON.parse silently rounds integers above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER: send big IDs as strings
text:
JSON.parse can change your ID without throwing an error.

JavaScript numbers are 64-bit floats, so integers are only exact up to 9007199254740991 (Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER). Past that, values get rounded:

JSON.parse('{"id":9007199254740993}').id
// 9007199254740992

MDN's own example: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER + 1 === Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER + 2 is true.

The reviver can't save you either. MDN notes it runs after parsing, so the number has already lost precision. Its advice: serialize large numbers as strings and revive them to BigInt.

My rule of thumb: any 64-bit ID (snowflake IDs, big database bigints) goes over the wire as a string, and I'd convert with BigInt(id) only if I need math on it.

Have you ever traced a "wrong record" bug back to a rounded ID?
